```{r panel-description, echo=FALSE}
description <- "
Panel F: The connectome predicts distinct population-level signatures
=====================================================================
3 biologically relevant encounter scenarios produce distinct mAL population
response patterns, computed from path strengths:

1. Female encounter:   ppk23 + ppk25 (contact with female fly)
2. cVA + male:         DA1 + ppk23 (olfactory + contact with male)
3. cVA + female:       DA1 + ppk23 + ppk25 (olfactory + contact with female)

Note: lone male encounter (ppk23 alone) is excluded because male contact
always co-occurs with cVA volatile pheromone.

Left:  Parallel coordinates plot (mAL subtypes as axes, 4 colored lines)
Right: Difference profiles between scenario pairs
"
pdir <- panel_plot_dir("panel_F_description", "txt")
writeLines(description, file.path(pdir, "panel_F_description.txt"))
cat(description)
```

## Build scenario data from path strengths

```{r scenario-data}
# Define the 3 scenarios (lone male excluded: male contact always co-occurs with cVA)
scenarios <- c(
  "Female encounter" = "ppk23+ppk25",
  "cVA + male"      = "DA1+ppk23",
  "cVA + female"    = "DA1+ppk23+ppk25"
)

scenario_colors <- c(
  "Female encounter" = "#D73027",
  "cVA + male"      = "#8E24AA",
  "cVA + female"    = "#F57C00"
)

# Build scenario matrix from signed activation (exc - inh path strengths)
# For multi-channel scenarios, sum the individual channel strengths
scenario_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = length(scenarios), ncol = length(mal_subtypes),
                       dimnames = list(names(scenarios), mal_subtypes))

for (i in seq_along(scenarios)) {
  channels <- strsplit(scenarios[i], "\\+")[[1]]
  for (ch in channels) {
    if (ch %in% colnames(mal_activation_matrix)) {
      scenario_mat[i, ] <- scenario_mat[i, ] + mal_activation_matrix[mal_subtypes, ch]
    }
  }
}

cat("Scenario matrix:\n")
print(round(scenario_mat, 4))
```

## Parallel coordinates plot

```{r parallel-coords, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
# Order subtypes by total activation across all scenarios (column sums)
col_sums <- colSums(scenario_mat)
ordered_subtypes <- names(sort(col_sums, decreasing = TRUE))

# Convert to long format for ggplot
scenario_long <- as.data.frame(scenario_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("scenario") %>%
  pivot_longer(-scenario, names_to = "subtype", values_to = "activation") %>%
  mutate(
    scenario = factor(scenario, levels = names(scenarios)),
    subtype  = factor(subtype, levels = ordered_subtypes)
  )

p_parallel <- ggplot(scenario_long,
                     aes(x = subtype, y = activation,
                         color = scenario, group = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  scale_color_manual(values = scenario_colors) +
  labs(x = "mAL subtype", y = "Net path strength (exc - inh)", color = "Encounter type") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 7),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_parallel, "panel_F_parallel_coordinates", width = 14, height = 6)
print(p_parallel)
```

## Signal flow model parallel coordinates

```{r sf-parallel-coords, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
# Build scenario matrix from signal flow model (matrix multiplication)
sf_scenario_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = length(scenarios), ncol = length(mal_subtypes),
                          dimnames = list(names(scenarios), mal_subtypes))

for (i in seq_along(scenarios)) {
  combo_name <- scenarios[i]
  dat <- mal_all_combos %>%
    filter(combination == combo_name, target_type %in% mal_subtypes)
  if (nrow(dat) > 0) {
    vals <- setNames(dat$net_input, dat$target_type)
    sf_scenario_mat[i, names(vals)] <- vals
  }
}

# Order by cVA + male net input (lowest to highest)
ordered_sf <- names(sort(sf_scenario_mat["cVA + male", ]))

sf_scenario_long <- as.data.frame(sf_scenario_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("scenario") %>%
  pivot_longer(-scenario, names_to = "subtype", values_to = "activation") %>%
  mutate(
    scenario = factor(scenario, levels = names(scenarios)),
    subtype  = factor(subtype, levels = ordered_sf)
  )

p_sf_parallel <- ggplot(sf_scenario_long,
                        aes(x = subtype, y = activation,
                            color = scenario, group = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  scale_color_manual(values = scenario_colors) +
  labs(x = "mAL subtype", y = "Signal flow net input", color = "Encounter type") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 7),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_sf_parallel, "panel_F_sf_parallel_coordinates", width = 14, height = 6)
print(p_sf_parallel)
```

## Scenario difference profiles

```{r scenario-diff, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
# Show how scenarios differ pairwise
diff_mat <- rbind(
  "cVA+female - cVA+male"  = scenario_mat["cVA + female", ] - scenario_mat["cVA + male", ],
  "cVA+female - Female"    = scenario_mat["cVA + female", ] - scenario_mat["Female encounter", ],
  "cVA+male - Female"      = scenario_mat["cVA + male", ] - scenario_mat["Female encounter", ]
)

diff_long <- as.data.frame(diff_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("contrast") %>%
  pivot_longer(-contrast, names_to = "subtype", values_to = "difference")

# Order subtypes by cVA+female - cVA+male difference (sex discrimination with cVA)
subtype_order <- names(sort(diff_mat["cVA+female - cVA+male", ]))
diff_long$subtype <- factor(diff_long$subtype, levels = subtype_order)
diff_long$contrast <- factor(diff_long$contrast,
                             levels = c("cVA+female - cVA+male", "cVA+female - Female",
                                        "cVA+male - Female"))

p_diff <- ggplot(diff_long, aes(x = subtype, y = difference, fill = contrast)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("cVA+female - cVA+male" = "#D73027",
                                "cVA+female - Female"   = "#8E24AA",
                                "cVA+male - Female"     = "#F57C00")) +
  labs(x = "mAL subtype", y = "Difference in net path strength",
       fill = "Contrast") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_diff, "panel_F_scenario_differences", width = 14, height = 6)
print(p_diff)
```

## Heatmap: scenario responses

```{r heatmap-scenarios, fig.width=14, fig.height=5}
max_abs <- max(abs(scenario_mat))
if (max_abs == 0) max_abs <- 1
breaks <- seq(-max_abs, max_abs, length.out = 101)
colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(100)

row_annot_sc <- data.frame(
  encounter = names(scenarios),
  row.names = names(scenarios)
)

col_annot_sc <- data.frame(
  row.names = colnames(scenario_mat)
)

ann_colors_sc <- list(
  encounter = scenario_colors
)

# Dynamic cellwidth based on number of mAL types
n_cols_sc <- ncol(scenario_mat)
cw_sc <- min(25, max(12, 600 / n_cols_sc))
fig_w_sc <- max(12, n_cols_sc * cw_sc / 72 + 4)

save_heatmap_fixed_annot(
  mat        = scenario_mat,
  row_annot  = row_annot_sc,
  col_annot  = col_annot_sc,
  ann_colors = ann_colors_sc,
  filename   = file.path(panel_plot_dir("panel_F_scenario_heatmap", "png"),
                         "panel_F_scenario_heatmap.png"),
  width      = fig_w_sc, height = 5,
  breaks     = breaks, color = colors,
  cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 10, fontsize_col = 6,
  border_color = NA, cellwidth = cw_sc, cellheight = 25
)

save_heatmap_fixed_annot(
  mat        = scenario_mat,
  row_annot  = row_annot_sc,
  col_annot  = col_annot_sc,
  ann_colors = ann_colors_sc,
  filename   = file.path(panel_plot_dir("panel_F_scenario_heatmap", "pdf"),
                         "panel_F_scenario_heatmap.pdf"),
  width      = fig_w_sc, height = 5,
  breaks     = breaks, color = colors,
  cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 10, fontsize_col = 6,
  border_color = NA, cellwidth = cw_sc, cellheight = 25
)
```

## Summary statistics

```{r summary-stats}
cat("\nActive subtypes per scenario (|strength| > 0.001):\n")
for (sc in rownames(scenario_mat)) {
  n_active <- sum(abs(scenario_mat[sc, ]) > 0.001)
  n_pos    <- sum(scenario_mat[sc, ] > 0.001)
  n_neg    <- sum(scenario_mat[sc, ] < -0.001)
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %d active (%d positive, %d negative)\n",
              sc, n_active, n_pos, n_neg))
}
```

## Panel narrative

```{r narrative, echo=FALSE}
# Compute scenario statistics
scenario_stats <- data.frame(
  scenario = rownames(scenario_mat),
  n_active = apply(abs(scenario_mat), 1, function(x) sum(x > 0.001)),
  n_pos    = apply(scenario_mat, 1, function(x) sum(x > 0.001)),
  n_neg    = apply(scenario_mat, 1, function(x) sum(x < -0.001)),
  mean_act = rowMeans(scenario_mat),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Cosine similarities between scenario pairs
cos_sim <- function(a, b) sum(a * b) / (sqrt(sum(a^2)) * sqrt(sum(b^2)))
sim_female_cva_male <- cos_sim(scenario_mat["Female encounter", ],
                               scenario_mat["cVA + male", ])
sim_female_cva_female <- cos_sim(scenario_mat["Female encounter", ],
                                  scenario_mat["cVA + female", ])
sim_cva_male_cva_female <- cos_sim(scenario_mat["cVA + male", ],
                                    scenario_mat["cVA + female", ])

most_active_scenario <- scenario_stats$scenario[which.max(scenario_stats$n_active)]
least_active_scenario <- scenario_stats$scenario[which.min(scenario_stats$n_active)]

# Which subtypes gain the most from ppk25 addition in cVA context
cva_sex_diff <- scenario_mat["cVA + female", ] - scenario_mat["cVA + male", ]
top_gainers <- names(sort(cva_sex_diff, decreasing = TRUE))[1:3]

narrative <- sprintf(
"PANEL F: Population Responses -- Distinct Encounter Signatures
================================================================

WHAT THIS PANEL SHOWS
---------------------
Top: Parallel coordinates showing each mAL subtype's predicted response
under three encounter scenarios:
  - Female encounter (red): ppk23 + ppk25 (contact with female)
  - cVA + male (purple): DA1 + ppk23 (volatile + male contact)
  - cVA + female (orange): DA1 + ppk23 + ppk25 (volatile + female contact)

Note: lone male encounter (ppk23 alone) is excluded because male contact
always co-occurs with cVA volatile pheromone in natural settings.

Bottom: Difference profiles showing what changes between scenarios:
  - cVA+female - cVA+male: the effect of adding ppk25 (sex discrimination with cVA)
  - cVA+female - Female: the effect of adding cVA to female contact
  - cVA+male - Female: pure cVA+male vs female contact contrast

KEY OBSERVATIONS
----------------
1. '%s' activates the most subtypes (%d); '%s' the fewest (%d).

2. Cosine similarity: female vs cVA+male = %.3f; female vs cVA+female = %.3f;
   cVA+male vs cVA+female = %.3f.

3. Subtypes gaining most from ppk25 addition (cVA+female vs cVA+male): %s.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
The mAL population does not report 'pheromone detected' but encodes
encounter type through distinct population patterns. The cVA+female vs
cVA+male difference reveals which subtypes carry the sex discrimination
signal when volatile context is present. The cVA contrasts highlight
DA1-responsive subtypes that shift the population code when volatile
pheromone is added to contact signals.
",
most_active_scenario, max(scenario_stats$n_active),
least_active_scenario, min(scenario_stats$n_active),
sim_female_cva_male, sim_female_cva_female, sim_cva_male_cva_female,
paste(top_gainers, collapse = ", ")
)

save_panel_narrative("panel_F", narrative)
cat(narrative)
```
